fr.recommendations:
• Mark the driveway entrance with reflective address numbers visible from the road in both directions.
• Trim vegetation along the access drive to maintain at least 14 feet of vertical clearance for responding apparatus.
• Cut back dense vegetation along both sides of the access drive to allow a responding vehicle to pass without obstruction.
• Clear a designated turnaround area at or near the main residence so apparatus can exit the property without backing onto the road.
• Mark or sign the secondary access point so responding crews can locate it quickly without searching.
• Keep the secondary access point unlocked and free of vehicles, equipment, or vegetation that would block entry.
• Trim any shrubs or low branches that block the line of sight between the access drive and the detached structure.
• Post the property address at the detached structure if it sits beyond the sight line of the main residence.
• Keep the walkway between the main residence and the detached structure clear of stored materials so crews can move between buildings on foot.
• Remove or relocate any parked vehicles that reduce the usable width of the access drive to less than 12 feet.
• Notify your local fire department of the solar panel system location and roof layout so crews have that information before an incident occurs.

wildfire.recommendations:
• Thin trees within the scattered cluster nearest to the structure to create more open space between individual trees.
• Remove shrubs growing directly against or immediately next to the structure.
• Keep low-hanging branches trimmed up from trees closest to the structure.
• Clear dead or dry plant material from underneath trees in the cluster near the structure.
• Maintain the open terrain areas between vegetation and the structure by keeping them free of debris and new plant growth.
• Keep both access routes clear of overhanging branches and encroaching vegetation along their edges.
